subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core expose cross-gateway session routing through session tools now, or hold this behind a separately designed federation/peer-gateway security contract?
rationale: The patch changes who may route session messages and spawn work across gateway trust boundaries, which automation cannot approve without maintainer intent on auth, identity, URL policy, and core-vs-bridge ownership.

options.title: Design the federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged until maintainers define peer identity, URL policy, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, then land a narrow implementation with proof.

options.title: Allow a narrow config-only peer path
options.body: Approve a smaller implementation that removes raw model-facing `gatewayUrl`, validates configured peers, requires explicit auth semantics, and proves two-gateway behavior.

options.title: Route the capability outside core
options.body: Keep core gateway-local for now and ask for a plugin or bridge design that uses current APIs or identifies the exact missing API seam.

recommendation.title: Design the federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR unmerged until maintainers define peer identity, URL policy, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, then land a narrow implementation with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history trail for gateway URL policy, session-tool behavior, and maintainer-facing docs points to this owner candidate.
